title: Atlasway partner outreach — raw notes
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad capturing account facts, hypotheses, outbound language and objection handling for Atlasway (regional retail platform). Low polish — for my own use and quick share with Jonah / Sofia.

Account summary (rough):
- Company: Atlasway — mid-size retail SaaS provider (inventory + POS + local logistics). HQ in Denver; scale across Mountain + Midwest.
- ARR: ~ $45M (public notes + pitch decks).
- Tech org: small central platform team (10–15), 3 product squads focused on storefront, inventory sync, and delivery ops.
- Current stack signals: Postgres primary, services on AWS (EKS), some TF infra. They use a mixture of vendor APIs (search, payments) — open to small pilots.
- Why they might care: customer support automation at scale, in-store agent prompts, automated product copy + localized returns messaging — all points where inference runtime economics matter.

Key contacts (first-pass research):
- Rachel Ortiz — Head of Product, storefront experience (LinkedIn note: ex-ecomm PM). Likely decision influencer for UX/perf.
- Dinesh Rao — Director, Platform Engineering. Responsible for infra choices; will push back on network/hardware changes.
- Priya Nair — Head of Customer Ops (sat in on their last earnings note about CX). Would directly own use-case outcomes.
- Champion candidate: senior PM or solutions person who cares about conversion lift from better product copy.

Top hypotheses / pain statements to test on intro call:
1) They are seeing high latency or cost when experimenting with personalization models — noisy A/Bs across SKUs.
2) They have an ops gap: infra team doesn’t want to self-manage LLM infra but needs predictable SLAs for feature teams.
3) Pilot with hosted API for quick wins then move to dedicated/reserved when throughput stabilizes.

Concrete outbound play (cold sequence -> discovery):
- Day 0 email (short): Subject: "Atlasway + Redwood — small pilot to reduce product copy time"
  Body bullets (short): quick intro (name + Redwood), 1-sentence value prop (reduce per-token cost, reliable latency), 1-sentence credibility (customers X reduced costs 40%), CTA: 15–20 min to show pilot plan.
- Follow-up 3 days: add a micro-case (one-liner example: "auto-generate 10k localized product descriptions per month at <1s tail latency").
- LinkedIn touch after 7 days + second follow-up.

Discovery call agenda (proposed 30 minutes):
- 5m: intros + confirm roles/goal for the call
- 8m: current workflow: how they generate product copy/personalization, current pain points (latency/cost/ops)
- 8m: show quick demo (hosted API + cost/latency numbers; sample prompt/pairing)
- 6m: pilot proposal (metrics, success criteria: latency SLO, unit cost target, conversion lift) + next steps

Sample outbound email (draft 1 — informal):
Hey Rachel —
I’m Maya on Redwood’s partnerships team. We help product-led teams get predictable, low-latency inference without the ops drag (hosted + dedicated + private options).
We recently helped a retail platform cut per-token spend ~35% while improving tail latency for their personalization endpoints — net: faster experiments and fewer rollout regressions.
Curious if you’re open to a 20-minute call to explore a small pilot (generate/localize product copy and a simple personalization endpoint)? I can share a one-page pilot plan.
Thanks,
Maya

Call script notes (cheat sheet):
- Start: "Two quick clarifying q’s: who owns infra-level SLA vs feature-level success for inference at Atlasway?"
- If they say "we own infra": emphasize Redwood Dedicated and integration options + autoscaling policy examples.
- If they say "feature teams handle it": emphasize hosted API for fast iteration + rollouts.
- Emphasize: we can run quick A/B on existing prompts and show delta in 2 weeks, no heavy infra changes required.

Objection handling (common quick counters):
- "We already have an LLM vendor": "Totally — many teams run 2+ providers. Redwood can reduce per-token cost via batching/caching and provide predictable tail latencies so your product teams can iterate faster; we can also run a side-by-side on a subset of traffic for 2 weeks."
- "Security/compliance concerns": "We offer Private deployments and VPC control plane + KMS integrations. For pilots we can do encrypted payloads and contract NDAs — then scope Private if needed."
- "We can’t change infra": "Start with hosted mode: same API, no infra change for them other than routing traffic. When ready, migrate to Dedicated with reservation contracts."
- "Pricing is uncertain": "Propose a fixed short-term pilot: capped monthly spend for 6–8 weeks with target KPIs; if we hit conversion/latency goals, we scope a longer reserved deal."

Pilot proposal (one-paragraph boil-down to send after discovery):
- 6-week pilot: run product-copy generation and one personalization endpoint. Scope: 2k prompts/day sample traffic (shadowing) -> 2 production endpoints. KPIs: 95th percentile latency < 500ms, unit cost < $0.0009/token (target), conversion lift >= 1.2% (or defined by them). Deliverables: weekly metric snapshots, evaluation prompts, rollback plan. Cost: capped $X (TBD) — offer co-funded pilot if procurement is slow.

Metrics to gather before pilot (prep asks):
- current traffic (calls/day) to candidate endpoints, average & 95th pct latency, current vendor and monthly spend, token sizes (avg & 95th), peak concurrency, and any hard SLOs.

Internal risks + red flags (note to self):
- Heavy legal on data residency — might need Private or on-prem clauses early.
- Platform team headcount low — if they need us to operate model infra fully, we should pitch Redwood Dedicated with strong integration support.
- Any antipatterns: they might expect instant large-scale cost reductions — calibrate expectations.

Next steps (my immediate todo):
- Jonah: share preliminary one-pager template (pilot + pricing) — due 2 days
- Sofia: review product-copy sample prompts & example outputs (deadline 3 days)
- Book exploratory with Rachel + Dinesh (aim for week of 2026-02-23) — include 20-min slot first.

Notes to self: keep outbound language very operational (latency/cost) + a clear low-effort pilot. Avoid generic "AI benefits" framing. If we get buy-in from product (Rachel), lock in an ops-focused stakeholder (Dinesh) before proposal.

Scratch rough prompts (for Sofia):
- "Rewrite product description for [SKU] to be more concise and conversion-focused, highlight shipping benefits, max 45 words."
- "Generate localized return-message in Spanish for [SKU], empathetic tone, 30–50 words, mention next steps to return."

Random brainstorm hooks (for outreach):
- "Turn your top 500 SKUs into local-language SEO titles in under an hour"
- "Reduce customer support handle time by surfacing suggested help responses in-store POS"

End of notes.
